# slopcheck

> CLI that catches hallucinated/slopsquatted PyPI and npm dependency names in requirements.txt, Pipfile, and package.json before you install them, checking each name against the real registry.

Use this after an LLM coding assistant adds or edits Python or npm
dependencies. Attackers have been shown to register the exact package
names LLMs hallucinate ahead of time ("slopsquatting"), so the first
person to blindly install the AI's suggestion gets whatever the
attacker put there. `slopcheck` flags names that don't exist on the
registry at all, names that exist but were published in the last 30
days (suspicious timing relative to an AI suggestion), and names only
resolvable via a private/extra index (unverified, not necessarily
hallucinated).

## Install
- [pip, from GitHub](https://github.com/experimental-gains/slopcheck#install): `pip install git+https://github.com/experimental-gains/slopcheck.git@v0.1.27` (not yet on PyPI — see the README for why the name is deliberately not fought for)
- [pre-commit hook](https://github.com/experimental-gains/slopcheck/blob/main/.pre-commit-hooks.yaml): scan on every commit
- [Claude Code / Copilot CLI plugin](https://github.com/experimental-gains/claude-plugins): `supplychain-guard` wraps this as an agent-triggered check

## Docs
- [README](https://github.com/experimental-gains/slopcheck/blob/main/README.md): full finding list (`not_found`/`recent`/`private`), `--fail-on` gate options, and verbatim pip/npm error strings this tool addresses

- [Source](https://github.com/experimental-gains/slopcheck): MIT-licensed, currently at v0.1.27
